opportunities.title: Fix the front door: a quote-first site and order-intake path that humans and AI assistants can actually use
opportunities.problem: The shop's only web front door is a 2022 GoDaddy brochure with no readable offer. The home page is a logo image plus one stock press photo with no service, address, phone, hours or call-to-action as text, no h1 and no meta description; the single intake is a Name/Email/Message box with no quantity, size, stock, deadline or artwork upload; no email address is published; the Google review profile appears unclaimed and its hours (9:00-6:00) contradict the shop's own (8:30-5:30), so a customer arriving 5:30-6:00 may find the door locked. Nothing on the site lets a customer - or an AI assistant shopping for them - get a price, send artwork, or book a pickup.
evidence: At 390 px the home page is a hamburger menu, the logo, one stock press photo and a '© 2022' footer - no address, phone, hours or service copy as text, page title is only the business name, no meta description, no h1 (https://downtownprint.com/)

The contact page has tel: links but only one form (Name/Email/Message, button 'SEND', reCAPTCHA) with no quote fields, quantities, turnaround or artwork upload, and publishes no email address (https://downtownprint.com/contact)
Triage agent-readiness scoring observed on the same pages: findable 1, answerable 1, bookable 0 - 'an agent cannot get a real estimate' (https://downtownprint.com/contact)
No prices, samples, brochure or downloadable content published; services are a flat bullet list on one page with no per-product pages (https://downtownprint.com/services)

Review profile is not claimed by the business owner and shows 3.8 stars from 29 reviews, with weekday hours listed an hour later than the shop's own site (https://reviews.birdeye.com/downtown-printing-center-inc-552901184)

Robots.txt is permissive ('User-agent: *' with no rules) and LocalBusiness JSON-LD exists, but the schema is not backed by readable service or price text on the page (https://downtownprint.com/robots.txt)
opportunities.agent_design: Agent-built, agent-maintained front door rather than a hand-coded redesign. (1) A content agent generates five to six real pages - digital copies/engineering prints, offset stationery and business cards, screen-printed apparel, signs and banners, binding/finishing, counter services - each with an h1 naming the product and New Brunswick, product-specific spec questions, published turnaround and schema (Product/Service/LocalBusiness) so Google and AI assistants can read and quote them. (2) A structured quote form (product, size, quantity, stock, deadline, artwork upload) replaces the free-text box and writes each submission into a quote queue; the agent acknowledges within minutes, states what is missing, and sets an expected-quote time. (3) A listing agent claims and normalizes the Google/Birdeye profile (one set of hours across site, schema and listings) and drafts replies to new reviews for owner approval - it never posts unapproved. (4) A visibility agent monitors how the shop appears to AI assistants and in 'print shop near me' style answers, and flags regressions. Human approves all published copy, prices, hours and every review reply. No payments taken in the pilot; the form stops at 'submit a quote request', not checkout.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A GoDaddy page builder cannot produce per-product schema, a quote queue that captures structured specs, artwork upload with size/format checks, or a listing-hours sync across Google, Birdeye and the site's JSON-LD. Off-the-shelf web-to-print storefronts assume a stocked catalogue with SKU pricing the shop does not publish, and none of them reconcile the review profile or keep content aligned as services change. The work is integration plus ongoing upkeep, not a template.

impact_estimate.range: About $1,000-$3,500/yr of counter staff time re-keyed from unstructured messages, plus an unquantified recovery of after-hours and 'is it open?' inquiries; no revenue uplift is claimed because no sourced benchmark for online print ordering exists for a shop this size.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference, not measured: staff currently spend roughly 1-3 hours a week reading free-text inquiries, asking follow-up questions and re-keying specs into a job ticket (profile notes the form has no spec, quantity or upload fields). That is 50-150 hours a year. Valued at the NJ median for Customer Service Representatives, $47,740/yr, i.e. about $23/hour over 2,080 hours. Assumes the structured form removes 80-100% of the spec-chasing hours but that total inquiry volume stays flat. The hours-conflict and unclaimed-profile items are stated as observed facts, not priced.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Two to three weeks: three to five live product pages with schema and a working structured quote form writing into a shared queue; Google/Birdeye profile claimed with hours, categories and services corrected; a simple review-reply queue for owner approval; a before/after report of what a customer and an AI assistant could read and do on the site versus today. Priced as a fixed-scope build with the content agent on AgentOps afterwards.

opportunities.title: Quote desk agent: turn the inbox and the counter into priced, spec-complete job requests
opportunities.problem: Every job starts as free text or a phone call. Staff must read a vague request ('some flyers for Friday'), go back to the customer for size, stock and quantity, price it by hand, re-key it into a job ticket, then chase the artwork - all inside a 8:30-17:30 weekday shift that is also handling Western Union transfers, passport photos and walk-in copies. The shop is open 8:30-5:30 with Saturday and Sunday zeroed in its schema, publishes no email and no callback commitment, so anything arriving after hours or mid-rush waits.
evidence: Only intake routes are a free-text message form or a phone call, with no way to send artwork, quantity or deadline - inference: staff re-key specs on every job (https://downtownprint.com/contact)

Hours are Mon-Fri 08:30-17:30 with Saturday and Sunday zeroed in the LocalBusiness schema, and hours are only stated as 'open today' text with no calendar or booking system (https://downtownprint.com/contact)

Front desk is interrupt-driven: alongside print jobs the same counter handles Western Union money transfers and passport photos, with the Western Union desk listed at Floor 1 of the same address (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Downtown+Printing+Center+46+Paterson+St+New+Brunswick+NJ)
Four production families - digital, offset/raised print, screen-printed apparel, signs - plus binding/finishing, each with different spec questions and turnaround (https://downtownprint.com/services)
Four decades of repeat work make the shop's own past jobs the best price reference, and none of it is published or searchable (https://downtownprint.com/about-us)
opportunities.agent_design: An event-driven intake-to-quote agent. Triggers: a new form submission, an inbound email, or a voicemail transcript. Steps: (1) extract product family, size, quantity, stock, colour sides, deadline and artwork status from whatever the customer wrote, asking at most two clarifying questions; (2) match the request to the closest historical job or price-grid entry and draft a quote with a clear price, turnaround and artwork spec; (3) attach the right production notes (bleed, stock, dye-lot for apparel, grommet/hem for banners) from the shop's own SOPs; (4) create a job ticket and, on approval, send the customer confirmation plus a pickup date; (5) follow up automatically on jobs stalled waiting for artwork and on quotes unanswered after three days. Human approval: the owner or counter lead approves every price before it leaves the shop for the first 60 days and thereafter only for non-standard or high-value jobs; the agent is not allowed to commit to a rush deadline it cannot verify against the day's production load.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A chatbot subscription cannot read a mailbox, extract structured specs from messy prose, price against a private grid and job history, write a job ticket, and then hold state for days waiting on artwork. It also needs guardrails: never quote below a floor, never promise a turnaround the press schedule cannot meet, and never send a price without approval during the guarded period. That is integration work against systems the shop already uses plus an evaluation harness on real past quotes.

impact_estimate.range: About $1,200-$4,000/yr of counter time at Customer Service Representative rates, or up to roughly $5,700/yr if the same hours are valued at the owner's time as a services salesperson; the larger, unquantified benefit is same-day quotes instead of next-day and fewer quotes lost to silence.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference: quoting, clarifying and re-keying consume roughly 3-8 hours a week today (one counter, four product families, no structured intake). A 25-40% reduction - i.e. 1-3 hours a week, or 50-150 hours a year - is transferred from the peer-reviewed QJE 2025 support-assistant study, which measured +15% issues resolved per hour for 5,172 agents, and from the Science 2023 study where ChatGPT access cut completion time 40% on 20-30 minute professional writing tasks; both settings are call-centre and simulated-task work, not a New Jersey print shop, so the transfer is deliberately discounted. Hourly value: $47,740 NJ median for Customer Service Representatives (~$23/hour) and $79,200 NJ median for Sales Representatives of Services (~$38/hour) for owner-attended quoting. No measured print-industry savings figure exists.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Three to four weeks: connect one mailbox plus the quote form; build a draft price grid from 30-50 of the shop's own past jobs across digital, offset and signs; run the agent in shadow mode for two weeks against real inquiries, with the owner approving every draft quote, then report spec-extraction accuracy, time-to-quote and staff minutes saved per job. Apparel and large-format quoting stay manual in the pilot because spec variance is highest there.

opportunities.title: Counter knowledge agent: the shop's own specs, prices and verification rules, answerable in seconds
opportunities.problem: Forty-plus years of operating knowledge - which stock is standard for which job, minimum quantities, which press takes which stock, how to price a short run of raised-print cards, what a passport photo needs, how to handle a controlled or regulated print order - lives in heads, binders and past job tickets. Nothing on the site states prices, samples, turnaround or specs, so the same questions arrive by phone and at the counter, and the shop has already lost a revenue line to a verification failure: a 2016 NJ consent order terminated its authorization to print prescription blanks after it filled 15,000+ blanks for people who were not licensed physicians without checking signature, licence status, identity or address of record.
evidence: 2016 NJ Division of Consumer Affairs final consent order: authorization as a prescription-blank vendor terminated after orders for 15,000+ blanks were filled for unlicensed persons, without verifying licensure, identity or address of record; sets re-application, audit and document-destruction conditions (https://www.nj.gov/oag/newsreleases16/Downtown-Printing_Final-Consent-Order.pdf)

The shop is absent from the state's current published list of approved prescription-blank printer vendors, so any regulated re-entry would start from a documented-verification position rather than memory (https://www.njconsumeraffairs.gov/dcu/Documents/NJPB-Printer-Vendor-List.pdf)
No prices, samples or downloadable specs are published anywhere on the site, and services are one flat bullet list rather than per-product detail (https://downtownprint.com/services)

Four production families plus binding/finishing and counter services, each with different stocks, minimums and finishing options - the spec surface is broad for a small counter team (https://downtownprint.com/services)
No careers page and no job postings found, so any new counter hire learns the spec and pricing rules informally at the counter (https://downtownprint.com/careers)
opportunities.agent_design: A retrieval agent over the shop's own documents, not a general chatbot. Ingest: price lists, paper/stock inventory sheets, supplier catalogues, past approved quotes and job tickets, press capability notes, finishing SOPs, and any controlled-print checklists. Two interfaces. (1) Staff-facing, on the counter PC and phone: 'what do we charge for 250 two-sided colour flyers on 100 lb gloss, and what is the standard stock?' - answers with the shop's own figure and the source document, and says 'not in the documents' rather than guessing. (2) Customer-facing FAQ answers on the new site, restricted to approved facts (turnaround, passport photo sizes, artwork file requirements, whether engineering prints are accepted), never quoting a price. A separate verification mode is offered if regulated or controlled print is ever re-entered: the agent walks the clerk through each required check - original signature, active licence lookup, identity of the person ordering and picking up, address of record - and refuses to release an order without a named human sign-off recorded against it. Human approves: every price answer above a set threshold stays read-only reference, and no document leaves the shop without the owner's sign-off on the source list.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: The value is entirely in the shop's private documents and its historical price and spec decisions, which no public model or generic assistant has. It also has to be trustworthy: a hallucinated stock or price becomes a misprinted job and a reprint at the shop's cost, and an invented compliance answer in a regulated category is a licensing risk. That means document ingestion, per-document permissions, citation-back-to-source, refusal behaviour, and an audit log - plus keeping the corpus current as suppliers change stock.

impact_estimate.range: About $1,200-$2,400/yr of counter time answering the same spec and price questions, plus faster onboarding of any new counter hire and a documented verification trail in regulated categories whose downside is not priced here.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference: the counter fields roughly 20-40 spec/price/policy questions a week across phone, walk-in and email (no call or ticket volumes are published, so this is an estimate). Assuming the agent deflects half and each answer takes about two minutes, that is 1-2 hours a week, or 50-100 hours a year, valued at the NJ median Customer Service Representative wage of $47,740 (~$23/hour). The 2016 consent order's actual cost is not quantified in any source - it removed a revenue line and imposed re-application and audit conditions, and that is described, not computed.

opportunities.pilot_scope: Three weeks: digitize the current price list, stock sheet and the four families' spec rules; stand up the staff-facing assistant over roughly 100-300 pages; test it against 40 real questions the counter actually gets, scoring correct / refused / wrong; publish the approved customer-facing FAQ answers on the new site. Regulated-print verification is documented as an optional module, not switched on in the pilot.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (22/30): the front-door failure is directly observed on every page and confirmed by two independent passes (triage scored evidence 5/5, and its one wrong_claim correction - that /contact does have tel: links - is folded in here, so the gap is stated as 'the home page has no phone, address or CTA as text', not 'no tap-to-call anywhere'). Counter-evidence that keeps this below 25: no call volumes, invoice data, employee count or revenue are published, so the internal quoting and knowledge pain is inference from the intake design and the interrupt-driven counter, not measurement. Fit (16/20): the gaps sit squarely in G, A and C, and all three can be sold from one build. Ability to pay (9/20): a single-storefront, owner-operated shop trading since 1977 with four printing lines and a Western Union counter implies real but modest budget; the only size estimate found (2-10 employees) is auto-generated and unverified, so this is deliberately scored low. Ease (12/15): one location, one counter, likely one decision maker, and a front-door rebuild plus a shadow-mode quote agent are well-trodden; the drag is that the owner is named only in a 2016 consent order and is not confirmed as current. Strategic (12/15): thousands of small commercial printers share this exact pattern - a page-builder site, a blind contact form and an unclaimed review profile - so the front-door plus quote-desk package is a repeatable vertical product, which is why the score is not lower despite the small ticket. No capability E opportunity is proposed: avenues.json is absent from this folder, so there is no verified hardware/design evidence to build on, the shop's actual press inventory is unknown (the site shows only a stock press photo), and the observed intake and front-door gaps are both cheaper to fix and demonstrably real. Total 71/100 - a warm, high-confidence-on-evidence but small-budget lead best opened in person.

best_evidence_signal: The home page carries no service, address, phone or hours as text and the only intake is a Name/Email/Message box with no quantity, size, deadline or artwork upload - triage scored the site findable 1, answerable 1, bookable 0, so neither a customer nor an AI assistant can get a price or send a spec (https://downtownprint.com/contact)
data_gaps: No call volume, quote volume, revenue, employee count or invoice data is published anywhere, so every internal-workload figure in the impact estimates is an inference from the intake design and hours, not a measurement.

The shop's estimating/job-ticket system (if any) is unknown - the site shows no CRM, ERP, e-commerce or file-upload tool, so the quote-desk integration surface is unverified and the pilot would have to discover it.
Complaint themes (wait times, responsiveness, pricing errors) could not be verified: the aggregator's 'more comments' link returned HTTP 403 and signed-out Google shows no review text.
The 2016 consent order names Juan Ruiz as Owner/President but there is no confirmation he is current, and no manager or staff is named on the shop's own site.
Whether the shop retains past job tickets and price lists in a digitizable form is unknown; the knowledge-agent pilot depends on it.
avenues.json was not present in this folder, so no physical/edge (capability E) opportunity is proposed and no walk-in equipment checks were specified.

No sourced benchmark for online print ordering adoption or per-quote time savings at a shop of this size was found; the print-industry quoting benchmark located in search was vendor-published and was not used.
